## Highlights

### 🐛 Games that aren't detected anymore
When a managed game was uninstalled or moved, or its launcher configuration removed (for example a Lutris game
config), NMA failed at startup with "Unable to find installation for Loadout". Its loadouts are now hidden until the
game is detected again, and the rest of the app works as usual.

### 🧹 Temporary files
Each NMA process now keeps its temporary files in its own folder, so one process can no longer delete the files
another one is using. Files left behind by a crash are still cleaned up at the next start.

### 🔧 Latest .NET 10 patch
The AppImage is now built with the latest .NET 10 SDK, so it ships the newest .NET 10 runtime patch instead of the
older one preinstalled on the build machines.

### 🏷️ NMA Community Edition name
The log files and the `plugins.txt` that NMA writes for Skyrim Special Edition and Fallout 4 now say
"NMA Community Edition" instead of "Nexus Mods App".

## Full changelog

- `fix(ui)` skip loadouts whose game isn't detected anymore
- `fix(ui)` don't restore the workspace of a loadout whose game isn't detected
- `fix(temp)` give each temporary file manager its own folder
- `chore` name NMA Community Edition in logs, plugins.txt and the CLI
- `ci` build the AppImage with the latest .NET 10 SDK
- `test(jobs)` end WaitForCancellationJob only through YieldAsync
- `docs` CLAUDE.md says the AppImage build installs the latest .NET 10 SDK

## Install

Download `NMAcommunity.App.x86_64.AppImage` below, `chmod +x`, run.
